correctness.rationale: The six-edge geometric partition is exhaustive; the segment obstructs exactly if its y=B crossing precedes its x=C crossing, equivalent to ad>bc. All possible nine pairings reduce to the explicitly computed baseline and four two-dimensional clipped product regions, yielding the exact probability. The two branches agree with first derivatives, the general transverse second-derivative difference is -D(C-D)^2/(BC^2), and square-notch Taylor expansions differ by 128h^4/3, giving the visibility fourth-derivative jump -128. Universal half-bound is a strict bipartition probability bound. A standalone checker independently tests six parameter choices by Monte Carlo and phase scaling; it does not prove the claims.

value.rationale: Independent contour samples give a physically natural visibility statistic for a nonconvex six-edge domain, mathematically different from area Beer index and invariant-line chord probabilities. The complete four-parameter exact law, sharp half-limit, and a phase-hypersurface C1 singularity with an exceptional symmetric C3-to-C4 transition quantify a genuine geometric threshold and can serve as a reference model for boundary-based visibility sensing.
